title: Sparkline Billing Handoff — compact pricing tiles and export patterns
creator: Asha Menon
description: Design and prototype a compact, exportable billing tile set (Sparkline Billing Handoff) for the Redwood Console. Deliver a set of reusable pricing UI patterns and CSV/Parquet export behavior for token-level breakdowns that PMs and billing engineers can ship in the next console release. Focus areas: dense per-invocation sparklines, attribution slices (route/model/variant), configurable rate preview, and guardrails for showing projected spend when toggling batching/quantization presets.
acceptance_criteria: Three compact tile variants (compact, expanded, and dense row) implemented as high-fidelity Figma frames
Tile shows per-route sparkline + 3-top attribution slices (model, route, prompt-size) with hover drilldown
Export flow produces CSV and Parquet with schema: timestamp, route, model_variant, tokens_in, tokens_out, cost_unit, cost_usd
Pricing preview control surfaces: rate toggle (sticky vs ephemeral), batching slider, and quantization hint show projected USD delta
Accessibility: tiles pass contrast and keyboard focus states and have screen-reader labels for sparkline summaries
design_decisions: Use tiny sparklines instead of full mini-charts to preserve vertical density in list views
Show top-3 attribution slices inline and allow full breakdown in a flyout to avoid clutter
Pricing preview will be eventually consistent: show simulated projection based on last 30-day distribution rather than attempting real-time recalculation
Export includes both raw rows (parquet) and pre-aggregated snapshots for quick downloads
Guardrails: when projected monthly spend delta > 20% surface a warning and require confirmation for plan changes
open_questions: Do we need per-customer rate templates embedded in the tile or accessed via the Rate Manager panel?
Should exported files include hashed prompt fingerprints to enable prompt-level audits without exposing sensitive content?
What is the acceptable sampling rate for sparklines on very high-cardinality routes to keep UI fast?
Is automatic rounding to 4 decimals for cost USD acceptable or do Finance teams require cents-level precision?
